category_title: Low-achieving students with disruptive behaviors and high absenteeism
minimal_context: The student is participating in a whole-class philosophical discussion about whether people need to have names.
dialogue:
TUTOR: Let's start our discussion on the topic of 'name'. Does anybody have to have a name?

STUDENT: Yes, we have to have names. If not, we could not differentiate people and it will be difficult to call people... when we call hey! All who are present will answer...

TUTOR: That is one answer. Now please stay quiet and listen so we can hear from the rest of the class.

STUDENT: (Stands up from his seat) Why should I stay quiet? And this is confusing anyway! (Turns to the student next to him) Hey, what are you looking at, stupid?

TUTOR: Please sit at your place and stop talking to your friends.

STUDENT: (Engages in a loud verbal argument with his friend) Shut up! I don't have to sit down! (Walks away from his desk towards the door) I'm getting out of this class.

options.A: Provide immediate verbal praise and positive reinforcement for the student's initial contribution to the philosophical discussion.
options.B: Allow the student to leave the classroom under the condition that he does not talk to his friends, and pause the discussion.
options.C: Facilitate the discussion and ask more probing questions so that students are able to clarify, justify, and defend their answers.
options.D: Describe an appropriate replacement skill and have the student practice this alternative positive behavior during the whole-class discussion.
